reading.body:
CyrusOne's Chandler campus publishes 169 MW of IT capacity across eight facilities, the largest disclosed data center campus in Arizona and one-third of the state's disclosed IT load.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 169 MW translates to roughly 4,200 racks; at 10 kW per rack for inference, roughly 16,900 racks. The same power envelope therefore supports very different AI compute footprints depending on workload intensity. Two million square feet of technical space gives the campus room to host that equipment, but the 169 MW figure, not the square footage, is the number that determines how many accelerators can run.

The campus holds SOC 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, ISO 27001, and TIA-942 certifications, which indicate it can host regulated financial, healthcare, and government workloads. However, the data does not identify tenants or confirm any AI deployment. Arizona's disclosed capacity is 512 MW across four facilities, but 57 facilities are mapped in the state and most do not publish power figures, so the state's actual data center footprint is larger and largely undisclosed.
